title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - streaming stability, roles, stop/logprobs, structured output
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: support roles parameter, stop sequences, logprobs passthrough, structured function_call responses and more stable streaming; no breaking changes expected for existing Redwood API consumers.
description:
Motivation: Some customers rely on OpenAI /v1/chat.completions semantics for migration and compatibility (roles, stop tokens, logprobs, and function/tool calling). This PR implements parity for the compatibility layer, fixes a couple of streaming edge cases (stale socket resends and partial JSON framing), and adds structured output support (function_call passthrough and deterministic JSONRenderer headers).

Summary of changes: - Add explicit handling for 'roles' and validate system/user/assistant mapping in openai_compat layer. - Implement stop token semantics (multiple stop strings, overlap handling) and ensure they are enforced both for sync and streaming responses. - Pass through 'logprobs' request and include token-level logprobs in the OpenAI-compatible response shape when models support it. - Structured output: add function_call field passthrough and deterministic JSON framing helpers so downstream SDKs can parse function call metadata from streaming chunks. - Streaming stability: fix socket reconnect logic that could accidentally resend in-flight partial chunks; add sequence numbers to streaming frames and a small client-compatible backpressure header. - Tests: new unit and integration tests for roles, stop, logprobs, function_call and streaming reassembly. - Docs: update docs/openai_compat.md and SDK quickstarts (python/typescript) with examples.

Implementation notes: - The compatibility layer (redwood/openai_compat.py) now normalizes incoming chat messages to our internal request model and maintains original role labels for response shaping. - stop sequence enforcement happens at the generator boundary to ensure tokens after a stop are not emitted; streaming frames include a 'stop_signal' boolean when a stop is detected. - logprobs are requested from the runtime when logprob passthrough is enabled; we aggregate token-level scores into the OpenAI response shape. - For function/tool calling we do not change the internal function execution flow; we only change the wire format to include 'function_call' hint and payload in the chat completions response as OpenAI expects. - Added a small compatibility shim for older clients that rely on empty "choices[n].delta" frames for function_call start.

Testing & rollout: - Unit tests added: tests/unit/test_openai_compat.py - Integration: perf-canary run against a staging model pool to validate streaming under load (latency and partial reconnection behavior). - CI: flakiness observed in early runs around websocket timeouts; increased test timeouts and added a deterministic reassembly test. - Rollout: feature gated behind 'openai_compat_v2' flag; gradual rollout to 10% of hosted traffic, monitor function_call metrics and error rates.

Related work: ENG-1452 (OpenAI compatibility parity epic), ENG-1460 (streaming reliability improvements), SUP-802 (customer support ticket requesting role/stop parity).
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) openai_compat: core mapping, stop/logprobs passthrough and unit tests; 2) streaming: sequence numbers, reconnect behavior fix, client header for backpressure; 3) docs and SDK examples + small lint/test fixes.
patch_snippets:
--- a/redwood/openai_compat.py
+++ b/redwood/openai_compat.py
@@ -120,6 +120,45 @@
 def _normalize_messages(messages):
-    # previous naive mapping
+    # preserve original roles; map to internal model but keep role labels for output shaping
+    normalized = []
+    for m in messages:
+        role = m.get('role')
+        if role not in ('system','user','assistant','tool'):
+            raise ValueError(f'unsupported role: {role}')
+        normalized.append({'role': role, 'content': m.get('content','')})
+    return normalized

--- a/redwood/streaming/protocol.py
+++ b/redwood/streaming/protocol.py
@@ -8,6 +8,18 @@
+class FrameV2:
+    def __init__(self, seq, payload, stop_signal=False):
+        self.seq = seq
+        self.payload = payload
+        self.stop_signal = stop_signal
+
+    def to_wire(self):
+        # small deterministic framing for clients to reassemble
+        return json.dumps({'seq': self.seq, 'payload': self.payload, 'stop': self.stop_signal})
review_comments: Jin Park: Please add clear validation/error message for unsupported role values (reject early).
Aisha Kapoor: Added strict validation and test coverage in test_openai_compat.py (see commit 2).
Miguel Alvarez: Streaming frames look good; is the seq monotonic under reconnects? Could this cause duplicate seq numbers when switching connections?
Aisha Kapoor: Sequence is per-request monotonic and the reconnect logic carries the last_seq to ensure resumed frames increment. Added integration test for reconnects.
Riya Shah: We need to ensure logprobs are only requested on models that support them to avoid perf penalty; gate by model capability.
Aisha Kapoor: Agree, added capability check and early-return in the runtime request path.
CI: initial run - unit tests failed (flaky websocket test).
Aisha Kapoor: Increased timeouts and added deterministic reassembly test to avoid flakiness; re-run CI.
CI: final run - all checks passed.
Jin Park: Approved - squash and merge when green.
merge_summary: Merged by squash on 2025-03-20. Merge method: squash. Commit message: 'openai(compat): add chat.completions parity (roles, stop, logprobs, streaming/stability, function_call passthrough)'. Feature gated under 'openai_compat_v2' for staged rollout.
notes_for_release: This release introduces OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity features behind a feature flag. Admins: enable openai_compat_v2 to expose full parity. Monitor new metrics: openai.compat.function_call.count, openai.compat.stop.triggers, streaming.reassembly.errors.
backfilled_docs: docs/openai_compat.md updated with examples for roles, stop sequences, logprobs, and function_call streaming parsing
examples/openai_chat_parity.md provides python/ts SDK snippets and caveats
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: partial streaming frames could break older SDKs. Mitigation: keep old framing for legacy clients, add 'compat_mode' header. Risk: logprobs add perf cost. Mitigation: gated by model capability and request flag, default off.
manual_steps: 1) Flip feature flag to 10% in staging via rollout UI. 2) Monitor metrics for 48h, then increase incrementally. 3) Notify support and update migration notes.
